newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP chooses new committee leaders.
newsitem.headline: EP chooses new committee leaders.

text.p: The European Parliament is due to complete its mid-term reshuffle on Thursday night by selecting new chairpersons for its 23 specialist committees.

The selections will conclude the mid-term changes, which saw the election on Tuesday of a new president and 14 new vice-presidents to run parliament's business until the end of the legislature in June 1999.
Subject to approval by the committees on Thursday night, the following new chairpersons are expected to take office:
Agriculture committee - Juan Colino Salamanca (Spanish Socialist)
Budget committee - Detlev Samland (German Socialist) (reelected)
Budget control committee - Dietmut Theato (German Christian Democrat (EPP)) (reelected)
Civil liberties and internal affairs committee - Hedy D'Ancona (Dutch Socialist)
Culture committee - Peter Pex (Dutch, EPP)
Development committee - Michel Rocard (French Socialist)
Economic and monetary affairs committee - Karl von Wogau (German, EPP) (reelected)
Energy, research and technological development committee - Umberto Scapagnini (Italian independent) (reelected)
Environment, public health and consumer protection committee - Ken Collins (British Socialist) (reelected)
External economic relations committee - Luciana Castellina (Italian United Left)
Fisheries committee - Carmen Fraga (Spanish, EPP)
Foreign, security and defence policy committee - Tom Spencer (British, EPP)
Human rights sub-committee - Andre Soulier (French, EPP) Institutional affairs committee - Biagio de Giovanni (Italian Socialist)
Legal affairs committee - Willy de Clercq (Belgian Socialist)
Monetary sub-committee - Christa Randzio-Platz (German Socialist) (reelected)
Petitions committee - Sandro Fontana (Italian, EPP)
Regional policy committee - Miguel Arias Canete (Spanish, EPP)
Rules and immunities committee - Ben Fayot (Luxembourg Socialist) (reelected)
Security and disarmament sub-committee - Jan Willem Bertens Dutch Liberal) (to be confirmed)
Social affairs committee - Stephen Hughes (British Socialist) (reelected)
Transport committee - Jean-Pierre Bazin (French, Union for Europe) (to be confirmed)
Women's rights committee - Nel van Dijk (Dutch Green) (reelected)
